title: Reconstruction of u from invertible finite reductions
statement: For the finite coefficient extension and coherent dualizing data of [def-sf-integral-finite-extension-core], if every normalized finite reduction of u is invertible, then u is invertible.

proof.text: Regard the scalar extension of wE.omega as a constructible integral object using sfIntegralScalarExtension_constructible. Form the prescribed finite counit family f0 and use finiteDualizing_reduction_coherent for all n <= m. The defining equation u_reduction, followed by cancellation of wL.reduction.hom, identifies f0 with the finite reductions of u.

The hypothesis makes every f0 n invertible. For their inverses, postcompose the required transition square with restriction of f0 n; functoriality and cancellation reduce it to the coherent square for f0. Apply integralConstructibleReductionHom to this compatible inverse family to obtain g.

Apply integralConstructibleReductionHom to the identity families on each endpoint. Functoriality of reduction and the inverse equations show that g followed by u and u followed by g have identity reductions. Uniqueness identifies these composites with the identities, yielding IsIso u. This also handles zero objects and the empty scheme without any extra hypothesis.
